eyebrow: Eat like a Phichit local · Updated 2026
intro: Phichit is a riverside city on the Nan River that has fed generations on freshwater fish — from crispy garlic-fried pla nuea on to huge pots of pla kang tom yam fragrant with galangal and lemongrass. We've picked 10 restaurants that Phichit locals genuinely take out-of-town friends to, spread across Phichit city, Pho Prathap Chang, Taphan Hin, and as far as Khao Sai–Thap Khlo. River fish shacks, old-school noodle shops, ancient coffee houses, and old-quarter snacks — all in one list.

blocks.html:
When people think of Phichit, they often think of the Chalawan legend — the great crocodile of the old Nan River that became the city's symbol. But what the river has truly given the people of Phichit is food. This city grew up on freshwater fish, so river fish shacks are its main event. Order garlic-fried pla nuea on, fish cake, then finish with a massive pot of tom yam — the whole table shares. In the city itself and in old neighborhoods like Wangkrot on the Nan riverbank, heirloom food vendors still hide in every corner, easy to find on a slow walk.

This list includes establishments that have been part of the city for decades. Krua Pla Yai at Thung Yai Junction in Pho Prathap Chang is the classic fish stop for drivers on the Phitsanulok–Nakhon Sawan road. Lung Waen River Fish in town is an air-conditioned, award-winning fish restaurant. Taphan Hin is a real food town: Siam Chuan Chim makes its noodles by hand, Koi Coffee is a heritage coffee shop that has been roasting its own beans at the old market for over 70 years, and Liang Hong Ki is an old-school Chinese restaurant where the hoi jo sells out every day. We close with Pa Thao's pork-filled sakhu drizzled with fresh coconut cream in the Wangkrot old quarter — three generations of the same recipe. Come to Phichit and eat your way through the whole list.

blocks.name: Krua Pla Yai
blocks.signature: Garlic-fried pla nuea on, pad cha pla kang, Nan river fish tom yam
blocks.descHtml:
If you're driving Highway 117 between Nakhon Sawan and Phitsanulok and hunger strikes near Phichit, "Krua Pla Yai" at Thung Yai Junction in Pho Prathap Chang District is the stop that locals and passing drivers both swear by. The restaurant does one thing: freshwater river fish — boiled, pounded, curried, fried — and does it very well. Great for families or groups who want to order a spread of dishes and share.

The dishes most often mentioned in reviews are garlic-fried pla nuea on, which many diners agree is fried crisp right to the bone and eaten whole, and pla ma tom yam, served in a large basin packed with generous chunks of fish in a herb-rich broth of galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaf. Some people find the tom yam leans slightly sweet. Pad cha pla kang and pla krai dishes are another strength, and the springy pla krai fish cakes draw many repeat orders. Fresh ingredients and punchy seasoning are the recurring themes in reviews.

Portions here are famously generous — a few dishes easily feed the table. Prices are moderate: fried fish starts around 150 THB while a big tom yam pot or prawn dishes go above 400 THB. Per-head average is roughly 150–250 THB. The restaurant is a single-story open-air building with wooden tables and fans; it can get warm at midday but the parking lot is spacious and easy to pull off the road into.

Open daily around 10:00–22:00. Note that portions really are large — don't over-order if the group is small. On weekends crowds build up, so expect a short wait. With fresh fish, generous quantities, and a convenient roadside location, it's no surprise this place has ranked near the top of Phichit lists for years.
blocks.spice: Adjustable — tom yam is mild to medium
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: tom yum · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Lung Waen River Fish
blocks.signature: Garlic-fried pla nuea on, pla krai fish cake, pla kaho tom yam
blocks.descHtml:
Ask any local in Phichit where to eat river fish and the name "Lung Waen River Fish — First Generation" comes up almost every time. The restaurant sits at a junction behind Happy Plaza on Saraluang Road in Phichit town — a made-to-order place that sources fresh local freshwater fish and cooks it simply, without over-seasoning. Ideal for families or friend groups who want to spread out and share several dishes.

The most-ordered dishes are garlic-fried pla nuea on (silky flesh, crispy skin, fragrant fried garlic), pla krai fish cake made fresh to order in each batch, and various tom yam — pla kod kang and pla kaphong both feature. The broth is hot and punchy with deep herb flavors. Multiple genuine reviews agree the fish is firm and fresh with no fishy smell, though the seasoning is bold and tastes best alongside a bowl of steamed rice. For a milder option, the pla kod kang curry and chuu chii are also available.

The setting is a shophouse restaurant with air-conditioned and fan-cooled sections, wooden tables and chairs — comfortable without the heat of a typical riverside fish shack. Price per head around 101–250 THB; signature dishes like fish cake and pad cha around 150 THB; tom yam and whole fried fish from 200 THB depending on size. Open daily roughly 10:00–21:00 (occasionally closed alternate Mondays — check their Facebook page first).

The restaurant's reputation is no accident. It holds top rankings on Thai review platforms, has received LINE MAN Wongnai Users' Choice recognition, and has been named a provincial highlight by the Phichit Chamber of Commerce. On holidays or in the evening the crowd builds fast and popular fish can sell out early since they use only daily-fresh stock — arriving during off-peak hours or calling ahead is worth it.
mustOrder: Pla kaphong / pla kod kang tom yam
blocks.bestFor: Family or group meal sharing multiple river-fish dishes, lunch or dinner
blocks.spice: Medium–bold (tom yam and pad cha are punchy)

blocks.name: Siam Chuan Chim Ba Mee Mueang Chalawan
blocks.signature: Dry Cantonese noodles with wonton and roast pork
blocks.descHtml:
If you're passing through Taphan Hin and want a proper bowl of noodles, "Siam Chuan Chim Ba Mee Mueang Chalawan" on Ruammit Road is the name Phichit people have been saying for decades. This restaurant has been open for over 40 years, ever since the original Hia Siam developed his own noodle recipe and began making fresh noodles in-house every day. The shop once appeared on the Khrua Khun Tor cooking programme, drawing visitors from all over. A great stop for anyone who wants to try an authentic local institution, or anyone on the Taphan Hin stretch looking for lunch.

The must-order is the dry Cantonese noodles with wonton — chewy, slightly springy hand-made noodles topped with fried garlic, blanched pak kwangtung, pork wontons, and roast pork that reviewers repeatedly confirm is real charcoal-roasted pork, not dyed red. The meat is sweet, tender, and mixes beautifully with the sauce. Also popular: dry tom yam noodles and pork wonton soup for those who prefer a broth.

Prices are very approachable — well under 100 THB per head, with most dishes around 35–40 THB. The shophouse setting is small and unpretentious. Google rating sits at 4.4 stars, high for a local noodle shop, with reviewers singling out the house-made noodles and roast pork.

Open Monday–Saturday roughly 10:30–14:00, and dishes typically sell out before midday. During busy periods expect a 25–30 minute wait. Regulars pre-order by phone at 089-564-4894. If you're making a special trip, arriving on the early side means you won't miss out on the noodles that put Chalawan town on the food map.
mustOrder: Dry Cantonese noodles with wonton and roast pork
blocks.bestFor: Lunch featuring the city's legendary noodles

blocks.name: Suan Ahan Khwan Khao
blocks.signature: Pla chon Khwan Khao, pla sap pad phrik thai sot, som tam cha-om kung, mango nam dok mai smoothie
blocks.descHtml:
Suan Ahan Khwan Khao is a wooden pavilion-style restaurant set in a garden on Srimala Road in Phichit city, a local staple for nearly thirty years. Locals turn to it first whenever there's a banquet, a family meal with elders, or a big group gathering. Multiple seating areas include air-conditioned rooms, wooden pavilions, and shaded garden tables that seat hundreds. Ideal for large parties or multi-generational families.

The dish at practically every table is pla chon Khwan Khao — a signature dish named after the restaurant itself. Equally mentioned in reviews is pla sap pad phrik thai sot (sautéed minced fish with fresh green peppercorns), fragrant and pleasantly addictive. For those who want a warming broth, the som tam cha-om kung hits a good balance of sour and rounded flavors. To close, mango nam dok mai pun (blended Nam Dok Mai mango) is praised as fragrant, sweet, and refreshing — a natural fit for Phichit's climate. The kitchen also does a Vietnamese-inspired naem nueng board and a range of Thai-Chinese-Vietnamese dishes.

Reviews consistently describe the flavors as homestyle Thai — not fiercely spicy, easy to eat across all ages. Many note that the food is good, prices are reasonable, and the staff is attentive. The garden pavilion setting feels relaxed even though the restaurant is large.

Open daily around 10:00–22:00. Easy to find in the city centre with parking available. On weekends and for large group bookings, calling ahead to reserve a table — especially if you want an air-conditioned room — is recommended.
mustOrder: Pla sap pad phrik thai sot
blocks.bestFor: Family banquet or large group meal

blocks.name: Koi Coffee (Koi 1)
blocks.signature: House-roasted heritage coffee, o-liang, khao moo daeng, khao moo krob
blocks.descHtml:
If you're up early walking the Taphan Hin old market and want to sit down with a cup of coffee the way Phichit people have drunk it for generations, "Koi Coffee" — or "Koi 1" as regulars call it — is the place to stop. The shop sits right at the market, at the foot of the bridge over the Nan River, and has been open for over fifty years. The founder, known as "Koi," started selling coffee from a stall at age eighteen, then passed down the recipe to his children, who still roast the beans themselves every day. Perfect for anyone who loves old-school atmosphere, vintage photography, and a cheap, filling breakfast.

The most popular orders are the house-roasted heritage coffee and o-liang (Thai iced black coffee). Multiple reviews say both are aromatic, smooth, and satisfying — the o-liang hits deep even without sugar. Quick rice dishes round out the menu: khao moo daeng (red pork rice), khao moo krob (crispy pork rice), and khao man kai (chicken rice). On some days there are pa thong ko (fried dough sticks) and khanom krop pak mo as a coffee side.

Prices are very gentle — well under 100 THB per head. Coffee costs just a few baht a cup. Regular customers drop in nearly every day just to chat. The setting is a classic old shophouse: wooden tables, wooden chairs, the smell of roasted coffee floating through the space. A favorite check-in spot for those who like vintage aesthetics. Open from early morning until evening — come on the early side.

The shop is small with limited seating. Mornings are packed and there may be a short queue. Parking is difficult in the old market area. In terms of taste, the clear strength is the coffee and the atmosphere; the rice dishes receive average marks in reviews. If you're here for great heritage coffee and old-shophouse ambience, you won't be disappointed.
blocks.bestFor: Morning coffee break + stroll through the old market
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: café · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

Staying in Phichit city puts you close to the Wangkrot old quarter and the in-town fish restaurants; staying near Taphan Hin works if that's your main food focus. blocks.name: Liang Hong Ki
blocks.signature: Hoi jo, pla hima steamed fish, tom yam fish
blocks.descHtml:
Liang Hong Ki is a heritage Chinese restaurant in Taphan Hin that has been open for over 30 years, passed from father to son. Many diners who came as children now bring their own kids to the same tables. If you want a full Chinese-style spread without waiting for a banquet invitation, this place covers it all. Ideal for family meals and groups who like to order several dishes for the table. On Thai review platforms it consistently ranks as Phichit Province's top Chinese restaurant.

The dish at practically every table is hoi jo — deep-fried, crispy outside, soft inside — the restaurant's best-seller. Another must is pla hima steamed in soy sauce: delicate fish flesh paired with wide rice noodles stir-fried over a charcoal wok. The clear-broth pla kaphong tom yam is another signature — bold and rounded. Also worth ordering: pad mi Hong Kong with pork floss, dried stir-fried fish maw, and cashew nut shrimp, all frequently mentioned by regulars.

Overall, reviewers describe the flavor as balanced and comparable to a quality Chinese restaurant. Some note specific dishes can lean slightly salty — diners who prefer lighter seasoning can ask. The two-storey shophouse has a comfortable air-conditioned floor upstairs for a longer, relaxed meal. Per-person cost roughly 200–300 THB per dish; budget around 250–500 THB per head depending on what you order — reasonable for a full Chinese spread.

Located in Taphan Hin town near Ko Sa Phan Bridge, about 30 km from Phichit city. Open daily, street parking available, accepts credit cards, and also caters banquets off-site. This place stays popular because it's the first name Taphan Hin residents think of for any celebration or quality Chinese meal. For large groups and holiday evenings, call ahead to reserve a table.
mustOrder: Pla hima steamed in soy sauce
Pad mi Hong Kong with pork floss
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: tom yum · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Krua Te Te River Fish
blocks.area: Khao Sai, Thap Khlo District, Phichit
blocks.signature: Pla krai fish cake, river fish tom yam, prawn wrapped in glass noodles
blocks.descHtml:
Driving north through Phichit near Khao Sai in Thap Khlo District when hunger hits — "Krua Te Te River Fish" is the one locals point to. It's a Thai-Chinese made-to-order restaurant with a focus on fresh river fish, sitting quietly along Route 11 (Highway 117 in the Khao Sai section) near a PTT petrol station before the Khao Sai intersection. Walk in and you'll find the tables nearly full. Great for families on a long drive who want a proper sit-down meal with air conditioning, or any group wanting to stop and eat well.

The most ordered and talked-about dishes are pla krai fish cake (springy, served with a peanut dipping sauce), river fish tom yam (many diners order the pla kod kang version — clear, hot, and invigorating), and prawn wrapped in glass noodles, a reliable order at this spot. For bold flavors there's also spicy sautéed fish, various yam salads, cashew nut chicken, and stir-fried fish maw with glass noodles, river prawn, and mushrooms — described in reviews as done well and not soggy.

Reviews consistently say the river fish is noticeably firmer and fresher than farmed fish, with seasoning that doesn't lean sweet the way city restaurants sometimes do. Many reviewers give high scores and say "for the price and quality this place is exceptional." Per-head cost 101–250 THB — good value for fresh produce. Parking is easy; open daily from mid-morning until evening. Each dish is cooked to order so allow a bit of extra time during busy periods. If you're passing this route, it's worth turning in.
blocks.bestFor: A proper meal mid-drive on the northern route, family groups
blocks.spice: Medium–spicy (yam salads / spicy sauté / tom yam)

blocks.name: Black Ground Cafe & Dining
blocks.signature: Freshly baked croissants and homemade cake served alongside coffee and hot mains
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Phichit city looking for a comfortable spot to sit down with a coffee, Black Ground Cafe & Dining on Saraluang Road is one of the most talked-about places in town. The interior is warm earth-tone brown that makes good use of natural light, with both a cool air-conditioned section and an open breezy corner. The smell of buttery pastries drifts from the oven as you walk in. The atmosphere suits working, meeting friends, or a relaxed family brunch.

The star of the show is the daily-fresh-baked bakery — especially the croissants, which many people name as their main reason for coming. Layers are crispy on the outside and soft inside with a clear butter aroma. For those with a sweet tooth there are several homemade cakes including a rich moist chocolate cake and a fragrant coconut cake that pairs beautifully with a hot coffee. Drinks are up to proper café standard; the signature iced options disappear down to the bottom of the glass before you notice.

What makes Black Ground different from a standard café is a full hot-food menu, including marinated braised pork ribs, khao soi, and bold Thai noodle dishes — so one visit covers a main course and dessert. Good for friend groups with different cravings, or families who want to settle in for a long meal. At lunchtime it fills up; large groups are advised to call ahead and book.

Central location, convenient parking, open from morning to evening. It has become one of Phichit's regular gathering spots. If you're visiting Chalawan city and want one café that handles both food and dessert, Black Ground won't let you down.
blocks.bestFor: Chilling with coffee, bakery treats, meeting friends, or a relaxed family brunch
blocks.zone: Saraluang Road, Nai Mueang sub-district (Phichit city centre)

blocks.name: Pa Thao Sakhu Sai Moo Wangkrot
blocks.area: Wangkrot old quarter, Ban Bung sub-district, Mueang Phichit District, Phichit
blocks.signature: Pork-filled sakhu drizzled with fresh coconut cream, served with fresh vegetables and bird's-eye chillies
blocks.descHtml:
If you're strolling through the Wangkrot old quarter on the Nan riverbank — just about 6 km from Phichit city — and you don't stop at Pa Thao's pork-filled sakhu, you haven't really arrived in Wangkrot. This heirloom vendor has passed its recipe down through three generations and appeared on Thai PBS's Naree Krajang programme. What makes people throughout the neighbourhood talk about it is that the sakhu here isn't served dry — it comes drenched in thick, fresh coconut cream before it reaches you. A must for anyone who wants to try an authentic local specialty impossible to find elsewhere.

There is essentially one item to order, but it delivers everything: pork-filled sakhu with fresh coconut cream. The tapioca pearls are translucent and pleasantly chewy; the filling is minced pork stir-fried with peanuts and fragrant preserved radish. Once the coconut cream is poured and topped with fried garlic, the result is savoury, gently rich, and well-rounded. Fresh vegetables and bird's-eye chillies on the side mean those who like heat can dial it up sharply. Everyone who has eaten here agrees: the filling is generous and well-seasoned — nothing like the plain sakhu elsewhere.

At around 20 THB a box it's a morning-to-midday snack that fills you up without breaking the budget. The stall occupies a small awning inside an atmospheric row of old wooden shophouses. Walk and eat, stop and photograph. Made daily with fresh ingredients; often sold out early because the queue never stops.

Open roughly 09:00–14:00 daily; the Wangkrot market is liveliest on Saturday–Sunday weekends. Arriving early is the safe play — Pa Thao's sakhu regularly sells out before closing time. One box is rarely enough.
mustOrder: Pork-filled sakhu with fresh coconut cream
blocks.bestFor: Morning or mid-morning snack while wandering the old market
blocks.spice: Mild — adjustable with fresh bird's-eye chillies
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: dessert · Ilya Plekhanov / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: Sanong Beef Ball Noodles
blocks.descHtml:
Walking through Phichit city on Charoen Si Road and craving a proper old-school bowl of beef noodles — Sanong Beef Ball Noodles is the name that Phichit people have mentioned for years. The shop tucks itself into a small alley behind Mae Thong Bang gold shop: a tiny shophouse with five or six tables, looking every bit its age as a decades-long local institution. Perfect for a quick, unfussy breakfast to midday meal.

The hero is the house-made beef balls — ordered as noodles or as kao lao (broth without noodles), and also sold by the kilogram to take home. Regulars typically order sen lek ruam (thin rice noodles with mixed beef) to get beef balls, braised beef, and fresh beef all in one bowl. Reviews say the broth has a clear, distinct beef aroma and the braised beef is stewed until perfectly tender. The balls use minimal starch, letting the meat speak. Some reviewers note the portions are generous to the point of struggling to finish; a few mention the fresh beef can be slightly chewy. Those who dislike offal can order kao lao ruam without it.

Very affordable: bowls from 40 THB, deluxe at 50–60 THB, with plain rice available as an add-on. Tea is priced at a few baht, classic old-shop style. Open from around 08:00 to 15:00 — closes when sold out. Come mid-morning rather than late for the full selection. The location is central, walkable from the market or the gold shop strip. Park nearby and walk in through the alley.

This place earns its spot on the Phichit must-try list by making beef balls from scratch every single day — honest, homestyle cooking that regulars keep coming back for. The shop is small and closes in the afternoon, so lunchtime can mean a short wait for a table. If you want beef balls to take home, let them know in advance.
mustOrder: Kao lao ruam with braised beef
blocks.bestFor: Breakfast or lunch for beef noodle fans

blocks.title: Good to Know Before Eating in Phichit

items.title: Having a car makes everything easier
items.text: The top restaurants are spread across multiple districts. Grab is available in Phichit but scarce outside the city centre. Renting a car or hiring a local driver is the most practical option. Most riverside fish shacks have spacious parking lots.

items.title: Always carry cash
items.text: Large fish shacks and established restaurants often accept PromptPay transfers, but street food vendors, snack stalls, heritage coffee shops, and old-quarter food spots frequently accept cash only. Keep small notes on you.

items.title: Timing matters
items.text: Morning items like Siam Chuan Chim noodles and Pa Thao's sakhu open in the morning and often sell out before midday — go late and you may miss them. Fish restaurants and garden restaurants stay open into the evening, so those are fine for dinner.

items.title: Share dishes for the best value
items.text: River fish restaurants and Chinese banquet tables are designed for sharing. Coming with a group and ordering many dishes to pass around means you get more variety and far better value.

items.title: Not every restaurant has an English menu
items.text: Local and heritage restaurants mostly have Thai-language menus. Try opening a photo of the dish or using a translation app to order. Phichit locals are friendly and happy to suggest the standouts.

items.title: Tipping is optional
items.text: Thai restaurants in general don't require a tip. Street food and snack stalls don't expect one either. At a sit-down restaurant with good service, rounding up or leaving a small amount is a kind gesture.

blocks.title: Making the Most of a Phichit Food Trip
blocks.html:
With a single day, split into two zones. Start in Taphan Hin: go to Siam Chuan Chim noodles first, since the shop opens mid-morning and often sells out before noon. Follow with Koi Coffee next to the old market — order heritage coffee and a khao moo krob and sit a while. In the evening shift over to Liang Hong Ki for Chinese: order hoi jo and steamed fish for the table.

If you're based in Phichit city, cover river fish properly. Lunch at Lung Waen River Fish or Suan Ahan Khwan Khao garden restaurant, then allow time in the afternoon to walk the Wangkrot old quarter on the Nan riverbank and try Pa Thao's sakhu drizzled with fresh coconut cream as a snack. Anyone driving the Phitsanulok–Nakhon Sawan route should know that Krua Pla Yai at Thung Yai Junction in Pho Prathap Chang is an easy pull-off for a proper fish-for-the-table spread.

blocks.text: With this many restaurants to visit in Phichit, staying a night is far more comfortable than driving everything in a day. Choose accommodation in Phichit city or Taphan Hin as your base and eat your way through the day without rushing.

faq.q: Which restaurant in Phichit is the most famous?
faq.a: For river fish, Krua Pla Yai at Thung Yai Junction in Pho Prathap Chang and Lung Waen River Fish in Phichit city are the two names that come up most often. In Taphan Hin, Siam Chuan Chim noodles, Koi Coffee (over 70 years old), and Liang Hong Ki Chinese restaurant are all well known.

faq.q: What food is Phichit famous for?
faq.a: Phichit is known for its Nan river fish. Key dishes to try are garlic-fried pla nuea on, pla krai fish cake, and a large-pot river fish tom yam. Beyond that: Taphan Hin's Chalawan noodles made with house-made noodles, Koi's heritage house-roasted coffee, and sakhu sai moo with fresh coconut cream in the Wangkrot old quarter.

faq.q: How much does it cost to eat in Phichit?
faq.a: It varies by restaurant type. Snacks and coffee like sakhu sai moo and Koi Coffee are in the tens of baht. Noodles and kuai tiao run about 35–80 THB per bowl. River fish restaurant dishes are around 150–450 THB. A full Chinese banquet-style meal at Liang Hong Ki runs about 250–500 THB per person.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table at Phichit restaurants?
faq.a: Most riverside fish shacks and snack stalls are walk-in. On long holidays, popular spots like Krua Pla Yai or Lung Waen fill up, so calling ahead if you're coming with a large group is sensible. For Chinese banquet-style dining at Liang Hong Ki, calling ahead to reserve is recommended.

faq.q: Which Phichit restaurants are open in the evening or late?
faq.a: River fish restaurants like Krua Pla Yai stay open into the evening, and Suan Ahan Khwan Khao is open late — both are good for dinner. However, some items only run morning to midday: Siam Chuan Chim noodles and Pa Thao's sakhu both sell out early. Plan your timing and you'll be able to hit everything.
